task.title: Show tooltips reliably in the desktop Next view
task.description:
The desktop shell's Next view (the cross-project list in desktop/src/renderer/app.js, renderNext and its helpers) has the same macOS tooltip bug the sidebar had: electron/electron#49843. When the pointer moves between different nodes inside one titled element, Chromium clears the tooltip and sets it again, and macOS then rarely shows it after the first hover.

Known sites, from the adversarial review of PR #180 (line numbers as of that branch):
- h2.next-group__name, the project heading: titled, with a dot, a key and bare text inside (~app.js:903-936).
- p.next-group__foot: titled, with children (~same range).
- The task rows (row.title = task.id) and their chips: titled, with child spans (~app.js:964-1003). Some children carry their own different title (the title span carries task.title, the age span updatedAt, the assigned chip 'Assigned'). That is an ordinary change of tooltip text and is fine. The bare children and text that share the row's title are the problem.

Fix it the way PR #180 did for the sidebar, keeping native tooltips:
- Children that only display (no title of their own, not interactive) take pointer-events: none.
- Bare text directly inside a titled element goes into a span.
- Nothing a click, keyboard or screen reader depends on may change.

PR #180's comment in desktop/src/renderer/styles.css, headed 'One node under the pointer', explains the rule. Extend desktop/test/sidebar-tooltips.test.js's guard, which today walks only #sidebar, to the Next view, or factor it so both use it. Dylan's hand check: hover a project heading, a group footer and several task rows repeatedly; each tooltip shows every time.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body:
Tested in current desktop release, tooltips seem to be working for me on the Next page, except for a weird bug where sometimes hovering over a task name shows that task name in a tooltip, and other times it shows the task ID.
Also, the only tooltips I see are either the task name repeated in the tooltip, or the text "running" when hovering over the project name. Neither of these are useful at all so maybe we don't need tooltips at all on this page, or we need to decide on better ones.
